artifacts.summary: Confirms task 982 is not blocked: the four review tasks (978-981) completed and the PR #7-#11 review round's rulings are recorded (two posted to GitHub, three fully decided but not yet posted); gives item-by-item findings and concrete edit targets for records/milestones.md, records/proof-mode.md, records/proof-mode-architecture.md, records/README.md, six named task descriptions, and a quoted /roadmap instruction, plus one found cross-record staleness (M17's stale 'under review' text in records/proof-mode.md after PR #7 merged).

memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic's records/ reconciliation work, a task description's own numbered 'open decision N' references can be stale relative to the current records/*.md open-decisions list: earlier review rounds (e.g. task 976) fold some open decisions into settled prose, shrinking and renumbering the list, while a task description written before that renumbering still cites the old numbers/content. When reconciling, map the task description's *content* (e.g. 'who drafts the semantic record') onto the current list by meaning, not by number, and treat a decision absent from the current list as already-resolved-into-prose rather than as missing work.

In a multi-PR collaborator review round gated through drafted-but-unposted GitHub review/comment text (specs/reviews/.../*.md), a dependent records-reconciliation task should treat a decision as 'recorded' once it is fully drafted and stated as a ruling (not a request) in the review artifacts, even if the GitHub posting action itself (a separate, user-gated step outside any agent's authority) has not yet happened. Blocking the reconciliation on the posting event conflates a mechanical publish step with the actual decision-recording event.
